title: 190-Year-Old DNA Revealed a Hidden Pangolin Species
mediaSource: pangolin close up scales, Himalayan pangolin Nepal India, museum pangolin specimen DNA research

scenes.title: A 190-year-old specimen revealed a hidden species
scenes.narration: DNA from a pangolin specimen kept in a museum for nearly 190 years has helped reveal the identity of a species that had been hiding in plain sight.

scenes.title: Scientists read DNA from an 1836 specimen
scenes.narration: Researchers extracted DNA from a historic pangolin specimen collected in 1836 and compared it with modern animals found in Nepal and northern India.

scenes.title: The modern animals matched it
scenes.narration: The comparison showed that pangolins from the Himalayan region belonged to the same lineage as the old museum specimen, resolving a long-running classification puzzle.

scenes.title: Its name is Manis aurita
scenes.narration: The species is called Manis aurita. It was once treated as a subspecies of the Chinese pangolin, but genetic and anatomical evidence now support recognizing it as a distinct species.

scenes.title: Why identifying the species matters
scenes.narration: Pangolins are among the world's most heavily trafficked mammals. Knowing exactly which species is involved can help trace seized scales back to the animals and regions being targeted.

scenes.title: Old museum DNA may help protect living animals
scenes.narration: A specimen collected almost two centuries ago has become a modern conservation tool. Museum collections can still hold clues that help protect species alive today.
